project.title: Archivio Associazione Luki Massa
project.description: METS metadata for the digitized archive of Luki Massa: 9,882 scans of lesbian and feminist activism, 1976-2015, described to Italian national guidelines and checked file by file.
project.introText: Metadata for the digitized archive of Luki Massa, which documents lesbian and feminist activism from 1976 to 2015 and was inventoried by Emanuela Fiorletta in 2023. I turned the team's cataloguing spreadsheets and the scans into METS records for long-term preservation.

gridImages.caption: Inside one METS record: header, EAD3 description, NISO MIX technical data, rights, files and the two structural maps, and how a single page links to its files, its technical data, its description and its rights.
Three levels: a record for each fascicolo, each series and the whole archive, each stored next to what it describes, with links relative to its own folder. All three levels link the same 9,882 files.
An excerpt of a real record: the unit's title, date and size (EAD3), the size, checksum and resolution of one file (NISO MIX), and the order of the unit's pages.

project.middleText: The records follow the Italian national guidelines for digitizing cultural heritage (ICDP, 2022): METS as the container, EAD3 for the archival description from the whole archive down to each page, NISO MIX for the technical data of every image and METS Rights for the rights. A Python pipeline reads the spreadsheets and the image files themselves, so every size and MD5 checksum comes from the real file, and validates each record against the official schemas. Comparing the sheets with the scans also turned up pages listed without a file, files without a row and names that did not match; the team corrected them and the records were rebuilt from the corrected catalogue.
project.highlightCaption: What the METS describe: the archive, its four scanned series, their subseries and all 85 fascicoli, sized by documentary units, and one path traced down to its files: a unit of nine pages, each a TIFF master and a JPEG copy with its checksum.
project.conclusionText: The hand-in is 90 METS files at three levels: one per archival file, one per series and one for the whole archive, each stored next to the images it describes, with every link checked against the archive's storage. Only what has been scanned is described: four series, from political and cultural activism to Luki Massa's personal papers and posters.

summary.brief: A digitized community archive that needed describing to national preservation standards.
summary.role: Metadata: the METS profile, the generation and validation pipeline, and the checks between catalogue and scans.
summary.method: Cataloguing spreadsheets and image files read by a Python pipeline into METS with EAD3, NISO MIX and METS Rights, validated against the official schemas.
summary.outcome: 90 valid METS records describing 85 archival files, 1,629 documentary units and 4,942 pages.
summary.stack: Python, lxml, METS, EAD3, NISO MIX 2.0, XML Schema

facts: images described, each with its size and MD5 checksum
METS records, none with validation errors
project.shows: A community archive described to national preservation standards, with every record checked against the files it points to.

decisions.choice: Describe only what has been scanned.
decisions.why: The records are for the digital copies: a description without images would promise material that is not there.
decisions.result: Four series are described; the one not yet digitized can be added when its scans exist.

decisions.choice: Take sizes, checksums and image data from the files themselves, not from the spreadsheets.
decisions.why: Preservation depends on knowing that each file is exactly the one described.
decisions.result: Every one of the 9,882 images has a verified MD5 checksum and its real technical data.

decisions.choice: Report mismatches between catalogue and scans to the team instead of patching them in the records.
decisions.why: The spreadsheets are the archive's catalogue, so corrections belong there.
decisions.result: The team corrected names and rows, and the records were regenerated from the corrected catalogue.

decisions.choice: Three levels of records: per archival file, per series and for the whole archive.
decisions.why: Each folder carries its own record, while the series and archive records give the whole structure in one place.
decisions.result: All three levels link exactly the same 9,882 images, checked automatically.
